reconcile.note: Gill treats the wicked's ruin as retributive substitution in judgment, distinct from the atoning ransom Christ pays for the righteous.

discrepancy.note: Strauss traces Matthew's ransom-logion to the same Hebrew notion behind Proverbs 21:18, where a substitute's death or ruin propitiates on another's behalf.

quotes.text: when in the first gospel ( xx. 28 ) Jesus says, he must give his life a ransom for many … this is doubtless to be referred to Isa. liii. , where, according to a notion current among the Hebrews ( Isa. xliii. 3 ; Prov. xxi. 18 ), the death of the servant of God is supposed to have a propitiatory relation to the rest of mankind.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §113, on Matthew 20:28 and Proverbs 21:18.

sides.snippet: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; The treacherous for the upright.
sides.verseText: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; The treacherous for the upright.

sides.snippet: For the Son of Man also came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
